I look around at my family gathered here. Bram's already off to the mine, muttering about copper and empty stores. Perrin's asking after food, and I've got nothing in my hands to give them.

In my day, we didn't let the young ones go hungry while we sat on our hands.

I watch the room as Bram admits what he's been hiding. The copper gone, the seam running pale, debt to Marta unpaid. He learned that from his father—work longer instead of speaking plain.

Ainsley's given bread already. Tobias is empty-handed and asking after food. And me? I've got one unit and work waiting at the carpentry.

"Tobias." I speak direct, no preamble. "Take my food. You need it for the farmland. I'll eat at the carpentry after I earn."

I hold out what I've got to Tobias, then I'm off to work. The debt to Marta needs settling, and Bram needs to learn what his father never did—say it at the table or don't say it at all.
